storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk this evening — skies are clear, radar is empty, and the cove will see the same quiet weather as the surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer in play: the Sound (66°F) is already slightly warmer than the air (64°F), and the gap only widens the wrong way to about −7°F by 7 PM as the air cools — nothing for it to act on tonight anyway.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: quiet. Radar shows no cells of 35 dBZ or stronger anywhere in range, there are no active NWS alerts, and the forecast is sunny this afternoon going mostly clear tonight with a steady south wind and no chance of rain through the evening.

Storm fuel: none. The model shows zero instability (CAPE 0 J/kg), and the NWS forecast discussion notes little instability for the next system to work with. Winds aloft are fairly strong (about 34 kt of shear from the west), but shear without instability does not produce storms.

Local effects: the cove's usual protection comes from cool Sound water holding a stable layer of air beneath incoming storms. That needs the air to be at least ~5°F warmer than the water. Today it is the other way round — water 66°F, air 64°F — and because the Sound holds its temperature while the air cools after sunset (6:26 PM), the gap goes further negative: about −2°F at 5 PM, −5°F at 6 PM, −7°F by 7 PM. There is no marine-layer buffer at any point in the window, and no sea breeze either: the south wind is the background (gradient) wind, not a thermal.

Most likely outcome: a dry, clear, breezy evening at the cove, the same as inland Greenwich and Stamford. With nothing approaching, the missing buffer does not matter tonight.

What would change the call: nothing on the horizon for this window. The south-to-southwest wind is running ahead of a system farther out; watch later forecasts rather than tonight's radar.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient southerly — no sea breeze in play

hourly.shift_note: slight back toward due S, gusts easing

wind.tactics_blurb: A steady 10–11 kt southerly blows straight up the cove axis, so pressure is even across the course and neither side is favored. Start mid-line, stay near the middle and play the small oscillations — and do not expect a sunset die-off, because this is gradient wind, not a sea breeze.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: a moderate gradient-wind evening with no sea breeze in play. A sea breeze needs the land air to be at least 5°F warmer than the Sound; today the air–water temperature difference is slightly negative (air 64°F, water 66°F, −1.3°F), so there is no thermal engine. The well-sited airport and buoy anemometers average 10 kt, and every part of the region from Boston to the south shore of Long Island is blowing S to SSW at 9–12 kt — that uniformity is the signature of background (gradient) flow.

Now at Riverside YC: S 188° at 10.7 kt, gusting 14, with a 10-minute average of 9.8 kt. The mid-Sound buoy is a touch stronger and more to the right — SSW 205° at 13 gusting 17 — though that reading is about 75 minutes old.

Will it hold: yes. Gradient wind does not depend on the sun, so there is no collapse at sunset (6:26 PM). Expect 10–11 kt through the whole window, with gusts easing a knot or two after dark as the air near the surface settles and the breeze gets smoother.

Where the pressure sits: due south is the cove's cleanest direction — the wind runs straight up the cove axis with no shelter from Greenwich Point, so pressure is even side to side. That is why the middle is the call. If the wind backs left of south for a while around 7 PM, the east side near Tod's Point gets slightly lighter; once it veers toward SSW later in the evening the flow stays clean with a little channeling along the west shore.

Shift character: small oscillations of about ±10° around south early, not a one-way shift. The model nudges the wind left to 179° by 7 PM, while the NWS forecast and the stations around the western Sound (already SSW 204°, 14° right of the model) point to a slow veer toward SSW by 9–10 PM. Net: steady near south through the 6 PM hour, then a gradual drift right late — a gradient-wind day, so the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply.

On the water: 10–11 kt gusting 14–15 is the top of the sweet spot for one-design dinghies — fully powered, hiking, flat water inside the cove. Cooling into the low 60s after sunset.

data_caveats: HRRR model data only reached 7 PM this run (forecast hours beyond f04 were not yet available) — the 8–10 PM wind rows are extrapolated from the gradient-wind trend and the NWS hourly forecast, so treat them as lower confidence.
Mid-Sound buoy 44040 reading is about 75 minutes old.
Model and stations differ slightly on direction: HRRR has S 190°, western-Sound stations are SSW 204°.
